title: VUA packages-ops result v0.6
description: Result documents for the packages-ops v0.6 write face slice F4 = repository lifecycle (proposal 027 freeze batch 2026-09-20; the v0.1 A1 removal result row, the v0.2 A2 install/upgrade result row, the v0.3 A3 registration result row, the v0.4 A4 repository add/remove result row and the v0.5 A5 project-creation result row stay frozen and served untouched). Envelope mirrors the standing wire shape (schemaVersion/operation/result); the envelope const is the word-list-row family version 0.6 and the result document carries its own family const vua.packages-ops/v0.6 — the two versions are independent (the c914cf2 standing rule). Operation/kind lock extended to twelve methods: BOTH preview methods are synchronous queries and answer kind=plan exactly (their failures are wire-envelope errors, not result arms); the apply methods, the A3 registration, ALL THREE A4 methods, the A5 creation and ALL THREE F4 methods are nine-state tasks whose terminal reflux answers kind=receipt / kind=rejected / kind=registered / kind=repoReceipt / kind=created / kind=enabled / kind=disabled / kind=refreshed respectively. The F4 receipts are the minimal honest audit shapes: kind=enabled and kind=disabled echo the request's repoId and NOTHING else (the port answers Result<(), _>: no payload exists; the state bit itself is read back on the packages-repos v0.2 subscription face, never duplicated onto the audit receipt — additionalProperties:false forbids inventing timestamps or state echoes); kind=refreshed echoes the repoId plus the REQUIRED cacheUpdated fact — the library's own update_cache two-arm outcome (true = the etag-conditional fetch wrote a new cache file; false = etag unchanged, 'already up to date'): BOTH arms are success and the fact is the honest outcome, never an error and never padded into a fetched-byte count or a fetched-package list (invented fields are INVALID by schema). Key sets: enabled/disabled share {schemaVersion, kind, repoId} with the A4 removed arm and are discriminated by the kind const (each $def pins its kind); refreshed adds exactly cacheUpdated; every F4 receipt arm's key set stays disjoint-from-invention against every prior arm. kind=rejected: the typed guard refusal evaluated INSIDE the task; the guard closed set stands at the A1/A2 three values — F4 adds NO guard: lifecycle refusals are backend answers and every one folds into execution_failed carrying the ORIGINAL port code inside detail as honest provenance (the A1/A2/A3/A4/A5 discipline). THE F4 PORT-CODE CLOSED SET IS THREE EXISTING CODES, ZERO NEW (all three were minted with the A4 batch and are reused here — the freeze transports their honest faces, it mints no code): vua.vpm.repo_not_found (an unknown repoId — no subscription row carries it; the A4 removeRepo same fact), vua.vpm.repo_write_failed (the VUA-owned state-file write-back failed for enable/disable, or the cache write-back failed for refresh), vua.vpm.repo_fetch_failed (the refresh network segment failed — refresh only). THE REUSED vua.vpm.* CODES NEVER TRAVEL INSIDE A REJECTED DOCUMENT (the code key stays pattern-locked to ^vua\.packages\.). Capability absence never reaches a task: the wire gate answers the generic capability_missing as an envelope error before submit (the gate reads the NEW defaulted accessor repo_lifecycle_capabilities() three independent bits — enable_repo / disable_repo / refresh_repo; default declared-none, ORC-DEV-004; the VrcGetLib override lands with the environment implementation-verification slice, the CLI backend has no lifecycle face and stays honestly false). additionalProperties:false everywhere is the false-assertion guard: facts with no port carrier (toggle timestamps, previous-state echoes, fetch byte counts, package lists touched) are INVALID by schema, not merely discouraged.

packageId.description: The VPM package identifier (the manifest name). No tighter pattern is frozen: the word list transports facts, it does not re-litigate upstream id grammar.

version.description: Target version for installs; null for removals (port fact: Option, verbatim).

reason.description: Machine reason, e.g. transitive_dependency, conflict; null when the backend carries none (port fact: Option, verbatim).

items.description: Every change the request would make (ORC-WF-002: the plan must cover every change the backend will make). On the install face this includes transitive dependency installs and conflict-triggered remove rows.

conflicts.description: Free-text machine reasons for dependency breakage the change would cause — the transparency face; the confirm UI must warn, the authoritative verdict stays server-side.

destructive.description: True when the change set contains conflicts or legacy removals (ADR-0006) — the confirm UI must warn; a false assertion is checkable against the other faces.

digest.description: FNV-1a over the canonical item list; the applyInstall confirmedDigest binds to exactly this value. NOTE (consumer narrowing): the v0.1..v0.6 plan shapes share the same key set — narrow by the schemaVersion literal, not by keys alone.

confirmedDigest.description: The digest the user confirmed, echoed — the audit link between the confirmation face and the executed result.

requestedPackageIds.description: The explicit request list, verbatim — the change list half of the audit receipt (the A1 removal variant; key set disjoint from installReceipt, registerReceipt, the A4 arms, the A5 created arm and the F4 arms).

removedItems.description: What the backend actually removed (port apply_remove {removed: items} verbatim) — the actual-result half of the audit receipt.

confirmedDigest.description: The digest the user confirmed, echoed — the audit link between the confirmation face and the executed result.

version.description: The request's version-selection fact, verbatim: null = resolver-picked, a string = the pin.

requestedPackages.description: The explicit request rows, verbatim (version-selection semantics included) — the change list half of the audit receipt (the A2 install variant; key set disjoint from removeReceipt, registerReceipt, the A4 arms, the A5 created arm and the F4 arms).

appliedItems.description: What the backend actually applied (port apply_install {applied: items} verbatim) — the actual-result half of the audit receipt. No minimum is invented: an honestly empty array transports as an empty array.

packageRoot.description: The request's packageRoot, echoed — the only fact the face has (the port answers Result<(), _>: no applied/removed payload exists, and the idempotent AlreadyAdded collapse means there is no first-vs-repeat fact either; additionalProperties:false forbids inventing one). Key set disjoint from removeReceipt, installReceipt, the A4 arms, the A5 created arm and the F4 arms.

url.description: The request's url, echoed — the audit fact (the port answers Result<(), _>: no payload exists; additionalProperties:false forbids inventing more). Key set disjoint from localRepoAdded, repoRemoved, projectCreated, the F4 arms and every prior receipt arm.

path.description: The request's path, echoed — the audit fact (the port answers Result<(), _>: no payload exists; additionalProperties:false forbids inventing more). Key set disjoint from remoteRepoAdded, repoRemoved, projectCreated, the F4 arms and every prior receipt arm.

repoId.description: The removed row's repository id, echoed — the one fact the face has (the port answers Result<(), _>: the id is already the request's identifying fact, the echo IS the audit link; no removed-row snapshot is invented — a row may carry absent-id facts this face never round-trips). Discriminated from the F4 enabled/disabled arms by the kind const, never by keys.

projectId.description: The port ProjectRef.id, echoed verbatim — the creation fact the backend minted (an informational identifier; NOT the 013 project identity key: the project identity stays the path). The ONE packages-ops receipt with an actual-result payload: the create_project port answers Result<ProjectRef, _>, and this key set is exactly that projection's first half. Key set disjoint from every prior receipt arm.

projectPath.description: The port ProjectRef.root, echoed verbatim — the new project's root directory, identical to its registered-project path identity: the REGISTERS-IN-STORE side effect is the frozen port fact (both backends' success paths tail-call FileSystemProjectStore::initialize), so a created project IS a registered project and the registered-project list shows it on next refresh (no 'directory-only, unregistered' shape is invented). Key set disjoint from every prior receipt arm.

repoId.description: The enabled row's repository id, echoed — the one fact the face has (the port answers Result<(), _>: the echo IS the audit link, the A4 removed-arm isomorph). The new state itself is read back on the packages-repos v0.2 subscription face (the REQUIRED enabled bit) — the audit receipt never duplicates it, and additionalProperties:false forbids inventing toggle timestamps or previous-state echoes. Discriminated from the A4 removed and the F4 disabled arms by the kind const, never by keys.

The disabled row's repository id, echoed — the one fact the face has (the port answers Result<(), _>: the echo IS the audit link, the A4 removed-arm isomorph). The disabled row leaves the package-collection world but stays on the subscription face with its v0.2 state bit. Discriminated from the A4 removed and the F4 enabled arms by the kind const, never by keys.
The refreshed row's repository id, echoed — the audit link.

cacheUpdated.description: The REQUIRED refresh-outcome fact — the library's own update_cache two-arm outcome: true = the etag-conditional fetch wrote a new cache file (settings userRepos[i].localPath); false = the etag was unchanged, 'already up to date'. BOTH arms are SUCCESS: 'no new data' is a refresh outcome, never an error. The fact has a port carrier (RepoRefreshOutcomeV01.cache_updated) — a receipt without it is INVALID by schema, and so is a receipt padded with fetched-byte counts or fetched-package lists (additionalProperties:false).

detail.description: Free-text provenance. On the F4 face every port refusal folds here with the ORIGINAL port code carried verbatim (vua.vpm.repo_not_found — an unknown repoId, no subscription row carries it; vua.vpm.repo_write_failed — the VUA-owned state-file write-back failed for enable/disable, or the cache write-back failed for refresh; vua.vpm.repo_fetch_failed — the refresh network segment failed) plus the reason — the reused vua.vpm.* codes never travel in the code key (the 013 reuse-code law: the pattern above stays locked to the vua.packages. family).
